commits.messageBody:
…ip sign can sign bundles

Every macOS bundle pulp_add_plugin() builds (VST3, CLAP, AU, AUv3, AAX,
Standalone, the AUv3 framework) carried <target>.inspector-capabilities.json,
<stem>.control-shipping.json and <stem>.control-shipping-report.json in
Contents/MacOS. Apple reserves that directory for code: an ordinary, non
--deep signature, which is what `pulp ship sign` makes, fails with "code
object is not signed at all / In subcomponent: ...json". `pulp ship sign
--identity - --path` failed on CLAP, VST3 and AU this way; only the combined
installer worked, by moving the files aside at sign time.

The sidecars now go to Contents/Resources (Versions/A/Resources for a
framework); plain executables and iOS shallow bundles keep them beside the
binary. Copies an older SDK left in Contents/MacOS are removed by the
POST_BUILD step and by the scan-stamp step, whose stamp name carries the
layout so Make and Xcode trees heal without a relink. Readers resolve the
location through new pure helpers, pulp::inspect::control_sidecar_directories
and control_sidecar_executable_directory: a standalone's control endpoint and
`pulp inspect audit` read Contents/Resources first and still accept the old
location. The audit never follows a symlinked Contents/Resources or
Contents/MacOS, and treats copies in both places as ambiguous in both modes.
build_combined_installer.sh no longer moves the files; it refuses, before
signing, any input that carries them outside a Resources directory, nested
bundles included.

Tests: new ctest macos-plugin-bundle-signing signs the fixture's Standalone,
VST3, CLAP and AU copies inside out without --deep and verifies them strictly
(fails with a JSON put back in Contents/MacOS); helper unit tests; audit tests
for the new layout, the legacy layout, both copies, and the two symlink
repros (break-confirmed); combined-installer tests for the new layout and the
refusal. After the change `pulp ship sign --identity -` signs CLAP, VST3, AU
and the .app and `codesign --verify --deep --strict` passes. Migration note
folded into v0.949.1.

Skill-Update: skip skill=upgrade reason="a routine migration-note section (v0.949.1); no new upgrade-skill workflow or gotcha"

## fable-graph review of 8850b1184d3ebc0015d2b41359ac797c64aac7cc: CHANGES REQUESTED (the dispatch half of the ruling is missing; two smaller items)

What matches the ruling, verified at the head: `intel-portability.yml`, `scene3d-advisory.yml`, `examples-validation.yml` are `schedule` + `workflow_dispatch` only; `control-shipping-native.yml` is path-filtered `push: main` + dispatch; `coverage.yml` has no `pull_request` and `max-parallel: 2` on its matrix; `sanitizers.yml` keeps `pull_request` only for `core/**` with `types: [opened, synchronize, ready_for_review]`, ASan and UBSan gated on `draft == false`, TSan `if: github.event_name != 'pull_request'`. Tests pin all of that (`AdvisoryMacOSCadenceTests`, the sanitizer trigger test, the build-dirs path contract). Required checks are all success on the exact head. Good.

**1. Dispatch-at-arm is not implemented, and the docs say it is.** The ruling's (b) had two halves: no `pull_request` on advisory lanes, AND the ship path dispatches each lane once at ARM time on the approved head, so a PR still gets its advisory signal before landing. This PR has no ship-path or Shipyard change and references no Shipyard PR, yet `.agents/skills/ci/SKILL.md` and `docs/guides/test-lanes.md` now state that these lanes are "dispatched by Shipyard at arm time". That sentence is false on main the moment this merges, and a skill is where the next agent will read it. Required, one of: (a) a Pulp-side dispatcher the ship path and `pulp pr` call (e.g. `tools/scripts/dispatch_advisory_lanes.sh <head-sha>` issuing `workflow run` for the five lanes, with a test), or (b) the Shipyard PR that performs the dispatch, open and linked in this PR's body, with the skill and guide text changed to say the dispatch lands with that PR and naming the interim gap (advisory signal only nightly on main until then). Landing the trigger removal first is acceptable for Daniel's capacity goal; landing a skill that describes a mechanism that does not exist is not.

**2. `coverage.yml` keeps `push: branches: [main]`.** That is one two-leg hosted-macOS run per merge to main, on top of the 3x/day schedule; the ruling was nightly on main plus dispatch. Either drop `push: main` (the 8-hourly schedule already covers main drift and codecov) or state the reason in `test-lanes.md` (e.g. per-commit codecov baseline) and count it in the expected load.

**3. Evidence.** `before-...T100831Z.json` is a dict with `measured_at`, `pulp_active_workflow_runs`, `vellum_active_workflow_runs`; `after-...T101846Z.json` is a bare list of 100 items with no timestamp, a different schema, captured ten minutes later and before any change. Both are pre-change baselines. Relabel them as such, give the second the same schema, and add the measurement that the ruling actually asked for as a follow-up task in the PR body: hosted-macOS running+queued and Vellum's required-check queue wait at the same hour of day after merge. Minor: the sanitizer `max-parallel: 2` is on `resolve-runners`' strategy, which the test comment itself says has no effect on the independent sanitizer legs; either remove it or keep it with that comment in the workflow, not only in the test, so nobody reads it as a cap.

No `reviewed:` line; this head is not approved. Items 2 and 3 are small; item 1 is the one that matters.

## fable-graph review of b2700a9aa49daa47ddd577340f466de1dd113580: CHANGES REQUESTED

Control first: `tartci host-profile --json` reports `reserved_gate_cores` 14 on m3 and 20 on m5s, so the guard's trigger is real on gate hosts. The setup.sh refusal and the hook path are driven through the real entry points in the tests. Good shape. Four items:

**1. The required gate is red on this head.** `Enforce version & skill sync` fails in "Gate-script fixture tests": `tools/scripts/test_text_encoding_lint.py::RepositoryTests::test_the_committed_baseline_matches_the_tree` (`lint.main(["--root", ROOT]) == 0` is `1`, job 114423336798). Run `python3 tools/scripts/text_encoding_lint.py --root .` on the branch and fix what it names in the five changed files. Suspect: the nested-quote f-strings `f"{bind}:{env["PATH"]}"` in both new tests. Those are PEP 701 (Python 3.12+) syntax and a SyntaxError on 3.9-3.11, which the hook's `${PYTHON}` on a macOS host may be; use a temporary variable. Required: gate green on the fixed head.

**2. The hook "refusal" does not refuse.** `shell-portability-hint.sh` is registered as a `PreToolUse` hook (.claude/settings.json:16-22, .codex/hooks.json:18-24). In Claude Code only exit code 2 blocks the tool call; any other non-zero exit is a non-blocking error whose stderr is shown while the command runs. So `exit 75` from `agent_build_guard.py` prints the message and the raw `cmake --build` proceeds on the gate host. The hook path must exit 2 to block (keep 75 for setup.sh, where the process exit itself is the refusal), the tests must assert 2, and the same must be verified for Codex's hook contract and stated in the PR.

**3. With a blocking exit, the match must be a command, not a substring.** `raw_cmake_build` matches `"cmake --build"` anywhere in the command text, so `grep "cmake --build" docs/x.md`, `git commit -m "... cmake --build ..."`, or an `echo` would be blocked on gate hosts once item 2 lands. Match `cmake` as the command token at the start of a pipeline segment (`(?:^|[;&|]\s*)(?:\S*/)?cmake\s+--build`) and exempt segments that are clearly not builds; add a test for the grep/commit-message false positive.

**4. setup.sh refuses `--dry-run` and `--print-plan` on gate hosts** (the test even asserts the dry-run refusal). A dry run builds nothing; refusing it hides the plan from the operator who most needs it on that host. Exempt `--dry-run` and `--print-plan` alongside `--deps-only`, and flip the test to assert the full non-dry setup is refused.

Minor: the override name `PULP_SETUP_ALLOW_FULL` doubles as the hook override; name the shared intent (`PULP_GATE_HOST_BUILD_OVERRIDE=1`) or document that one variable governs both. `Version-Bump: plugin=skip` is present; the skill map for `hooks/` and `tools/scripts/` did not trip skill-sync, fine.

No `reviewed:` line; this head is not approved.

## fable-graph review of e145e074b6031906e2a6f90ff4ebd1e1bd1ef976: content approved; `reviewed:` line follows when `macos` is green

All four items from b2700a9a are fixed as asked:

1. **Gate red:** `Enforce version & skill sync` is success on this head; the PEP 701 nested-quote f-strings are gone (`path_value` temporaries) and the subprocess calls pin `encoding="utf-8"`.
2. **The hook now blocks:** `shell-portability-hint.sh` exits 2 on a guard refusal, which is the only exit Claude Code treats as blocking for a PreToolUse hook; the real-hook test asserts 2.
3. **Command token, not substring:** `raw_cmake_build` is `(?:^|[;&|]\s*)(?:\S*/)?cmake\s+--build(?:\s|$)`, so `cmake` must open a shell segment. The real-hook test now proves `grep "cmake --build" ...`, `git commit -m "... cmake --build"` and `echo cmake --build ...` pass while `cmake --build build` is refused and `tools/ci/governed-build.sh cmake --build build` is allowed (governed-build opens the segment, so the regex never sees cmake first).
4. **setup.sh exempts `--dry-run` and `--print-plan`;** the test asserts the dry run is not refused, the plan prints, and the plain full setup is refused with the `--deps-only` / `pulp build` guidance.

Controls stand from the first review: `reserved_gate_cores` is 14 on m3 and 20 on m5s, so the trigger is real on gate hosts.

Should-fix-soon, not blocking: the token match misses the common accidental wrappers `time cmake --build`, `nice cmake --build`, `caffeinate cmake --build`, `env X=1 cmake --build`; allow an optional `(?:(?:time|nice|caffeinate|env(?:\s+\S+=\S+)*)\s+)*` prefix and add one test per wrapper. Also unverified from here: the Codex hook contract for exit 2; the PR should name the document or test that establishes it.
